lessons.title: Connect, Extend, and Unify
lessons.why: The model decides the media path and the licenses. The sales adjective does not.
body: Microsoft Learn, accessed 14 October 2026, names three models. Connect uses certified SBCs and Direct Routing. Extend uses the Teams client, Graph, and Cloud Communications APIs, with Teams Phone as the calling system. Unify is the native model. Partner text describes Unify as ACS-based applications on Teams calling infrastructure. Older decks say Power. Ask which current model the vendor holds.

In the Connect article, the contact-center agent does not need a phone-system license for that solution. A Teams user who receives a transfer does need Teams Phone and a number. Graph is not a SIP trunk. You still need a PSTN option.
lessons.say: I use Connect, Extend, and Unify. If someone says Power, I ask which current model they mean.
lessons.fault: The contract says Power and nobody opens the right ports.
lessons.listen: Name the model: Connect, Extend, or Unify. The media path and the licenses follow that name.

lessons.title: Teams Phone extensibility
lessons.why: It is how a contact center uses the Teams Phone you already paid for, instead of a second PBX.
body: Teams Phone extensibility, documented for ACS and announced for Dynamics 365 Contact Center and some Unify-certified ISVs, lets the agent’s telephony be Teams Phone. The announcement named a set of vendors. That set moves. Certification is still the bar if you want the supported experience. An API existing is not a finished certification.
Presence can be synced with Graph. Presence sync is not audio. Do not declare the integration done because a status bubble moves.

chart.title: Done means audio
chart.note: Presence is not the phone call.

lessons.say: Extensibility reuses Teams Phone. I want the vendor’s current certification, not only a presence sync.
lessons.fault: Two phones ring the same person, or only presence works.
lessons.listen: Teams Phone extensibility reuses Teams calling inside a certified contact center. Presence sync is not the audio path.

lessons.title: CUCM and CUBE
lessons.why: Most Teams migrations in a Cisco estate are a dual-run, not a weekend miracle.
body: A calling search space is closest to a voice routing policy’s ordered usages, and it is not a one-to-one object. A translation pattern is closest to a dial-plan rule. A route pattern is closest to a voice route. There is no partition object in Teams. Pick one system to normalize numbers.

Calls from people still on CUCM to people now on Teams trombone through CUBE. That is normal during dual-running and expensive as a steady state. Move groups that call each other in the same wave. Keep the old route until rollback is boring.

lessons.why: A split estate needs a voice bridge. Chat federation is a different project.
body: A SIP trunk through a local gateway or CUBE can carry calls between Webex Calling users and Teams users. Treat it as coexistence with one numbering plan. Two dial plans that both own a range will fail in both directions.
Do not describe that trunk as a merger, and do not assume meeting interop came along for free. Write which numbers remain on Webex and for how long.
lessons.say: Webex voice interop is a SIP bridge and a numbering plan, not a chat project.
lessons.fault: Both clouds believe they own the same range.
lessons.listen: Bridge Webex Calling and Teams with an SBC and one numbering owner. Keep chat interop as a separate decision.

lessons.title: UCCE during a move
lessons.why: Contact-center agents and knowledge workers should not be forced through the same weekend.
body: Leave UCCE agents on CVP and Finesse while knowledge workers move to Teams. The SBC sends contact-center numbers to CUCM and user numbers to Teams. A Teams client does not keep a CVP script in control of that agent.

Test a transfer from the contact center to an expert who now lives on Teams. That expert needs Teams Phone and a number. Then schedule the agent migration as its own project, with the certified contact-center model you actually bought.
lessons.say: I do not put UCCE agents on Teams and expect CVP to keep controlling them.
lessons.fault: Agents move first and the IVR can no longer see them.
lessons.listen: Move knowledge workers first if UCCE must stay. Split the dial plan by range, and license experts who receive transfers.

lessons.title: Genesys and Amazon Connect
lessons.why: Both appear in real estates. Neither is ‘a Microsoft feature’ you can assume.
body: Genesys sells Teams integrations. Ask which certification model they currently hold, because Connect, Extend, and Unify change the media path. A statement of work that says ‘certified’ and does not name the model is incomplete.

Amazon Connect is often bridged with SIP through an SBC or a voice connector. Design the path and the Call-ID you will store. If both platforms record, you still need one identifier that joins them. Confirm the current vendor document before you promise whisper, barge, or a particular recording mode.
lessons.say: I ask Genesys which model, and I draw the SIP path for Amazon Connect. I store a Call-ID either way.
lessons.fault: Both platforms record and neither capture has the Call-ID.
lessons.listen: Name the Genesys certification model. Draw the Amazon Connect SIP path. Keep a join key.
